patch_description: Keep the direct-demand reward, but add a congestion surrogate for pairs of links sharing a tail or a head. A node has only two outgoing and two incoming links, so selecting two links with high estimated traffic exposure at the same endpoint is a warning sign for an unbalanced topology. The exposure estimate combines direct demand on the link with a modest share of the relevant node’s total traffic, reflecting transit pressure. Positive pair costs discourage concentrating that pressure on a single node; the direct-demand reward still favors useful links. The number of added terms is O(n^3), within the limit, and the stronger degree penalty helps preserve feasible degree patterns before repair.
